question_template: How many complaints are pending department wise?
retrieval_text: how many complaints are pending department wise total open unresolved active backlog distribution by department punyat kiti complaints pending aahet vibhaganusar dakjava
sql_template:
SELECT d.department_name, d.department_name_mar, COUNT(*) AS pending
FROM complaint c
JOIN status_master s ON s.id = c.status_id AND s.is_terminal = false
JOIN department_master d ON d.id = c.department_id
GROUP BY d.id, d.department_name, d.department_name_mar
ORDER BY pending DESC;

question_template: Show pending complaints for {department} or {ward}.
retrieval_text: show pending open unresolved complaints for specific department ward or zone water supply drainage kothrud aundh pending count
sql_template:
SELECT d.department_name, w.ward_name, COUNT(*) AS pending
FROM complaint c
JOIN status_master s ON s.id = c.status_id AND s.is_terminal = false
JOIN department_master d ON d.id = c.department_id
JOIN ward_master w ON w.id = c.ward_id
WHERE (:department_id IS NULL OR c.department_id = :department_id)
  AND (:ward_id IS NULL OR c.ward_id = :ward_id)
GROUP BY d.department_name, w.ward_name
ORDER BY pending DESC;

question_template: What percentage of total complaints are currently pending?
retrieval_text: what percentage of total complaints are currently pending total open vs resolved ratio ratio percentage dakjava
sql_template:
SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.is_terminal = false) AS pending,
       COUNT(*) AS total,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.is_terminal = false) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1) AS pending_pct
FROM complaint c
JOIN status_master s ON s.id = c.status_id;

question_template: Which top {limit} officers are performing best or worst overall?
retrieval_text: which officers are performing best worst overall ranking resolved count avg resolution time slow fast officers best officer in pune hadapsar kothrud
sql_template:
SELECT u.full_name, u.designation, d.department_name,
       COUNT(*) AS resolved_count,
       ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(epoch FROM (c.resolved_at - c.created_at))/86400)::numeric, 1) AS avg_days
FROM complaint c
JOIN user_master u ON u.id = c.resolved_by_id
LEFT JOIN department_master d ON d.id = u.department_id
WHERE c.resolved_at IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY u.id, u.full_name, u.designation, d.department_name
ORDER BY resolved_count DESC
LIMIT :limit;

question_template: Which officers have the most SLA breaches?
retrieval_text: which officers have the most sla breaches overdue maximum breach counts worst performing officers
sql_template:
SELECT u.full_name, u.designation, COUNT(*) AS breaches
FROM complaint c
JOIN user_master u ON u.id = COALESCE(c.assigned_to_id, c.ward_officer_id)
WHERE c.sla_status = 'BREACHED'
GROUP BY u.id, u.full_name, u.designation
ORDER BY breaches DESC
LIMIT :limit;

question_template: Which officers have not resolved a single complaint in the last 30 days?
retrieval_text: which officers have not resolved a single complaint in last 30 days zero resolutions inactive officers audit list
sql_template:
SELECT u.full_name, u.designation, d.department_name
FROM user_master u
LEFT JOIN department_master d ON d.id = u.department_id
WHERE u.is_active = true
  AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM complaint c
      WHERE c.resolved_by_id = u.id
        AND c.resolved_at >= now() - interval '30 days'
  )
LIMIT :limit;

question_template: What is the overall SLA compliance rate citywide?
retrieval_text: what is the overall sla compliance rate percentage citywide meeting target total within deadline vs breached
sql_template:
SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND c.resolved_at <= c.sla_deadline) AS within_sla,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.resolved_at IS NOT NULL) AS total_resolved,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.resolved_at <= c.sla_deadline)
             / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.resolved_at IS NOT NULL), 0), 1) AS compliance_pct
FROM complaint c
WHERE c.sla_deadline IS NOT NULL;

question_template: How many complaints have breached SLA right now by department?
retrieval_text: how many complaints have breached sla right now department wise overdue count deadline crossed
sql_template:
SELECT d.department_name, COUNT(*) AS breached_count
FROM complaint c
JOIN status_master s ON s.id = c.status_id AND s.is_terminal = false
JOIN department_master d ON d.id = c.department_id
WHERE c.sla_status = 'BREACHED' OR c.sla_deadline < now()
GROUP BY d.department_name
ORDER BY breached_count DESC;

question_template: Show complaints reaching 75% or 90% of SLA time (critical list).
retrieval_text: show complaints reaching 75 90 percent of sla time critical near breach warning alert list
sql_template:
SELECT c.complaint_number, c.title, c.sla_deadline,
       ROUND(100.0 * EXTRACT(epoch FROM (now() - c.created_at))
             / NULLIF(EXTRACT(epoch FROM (c.sla_deadline - c.created_at)), 0)) AS sla_consumed_pct
FROM complaint c
JOIN status_master s ON s.id = c.status_id AND s.is_terminal = false
WHERE c.sla_deadline IS NOT NULL AND c.sla_deadline > now()
  AND (now() - c.created_at) >= 0.75 * (c.sla_deadline - c.created_at)
ORDER BY sla_consumed_pct DESC
LIMIT :limit;

question_template: Which ward has the worst or best SLA compliance?
retrieval_text: which ward has worst best sla compliance ranking ward wise percentage meeting deadline
sql_template:
SELECT w.ward_name,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.resolved_at <= c.sla_deadline) AS within_sla,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.resolved_at IS NOT NULL) AS total_resolved,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.resolved_at <= c.sla_deadline)
             / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.resolved_at IS NOT NULL), 0), 1) AS compliance_pct
FROM complaint c
JOIN ward_master w ON w.id = c.ward_id
WHERE w.ward_number IS NOT NULL AND c.sla_deadline IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY w.id, w.ward_name
ORDER BY compliance_pct ASC;

question_template: How many complaints got escalated department or level wise?
retrieval_text: how many complaints got escalated department level wise total escalation counts level 1 level 2 commissioner level
sql_template:
SELECT eh.to_level, COUNT(*) AS escalation_count
FROM escalation_history eh
JOIN complaint c ON c.id = eh.complaint_id
GROUP BY eh.to_level
ORDER BY escalation_count DESC;

question_template: Which complaints have been escalated twice or more?
retrieval_text: which complaints have been escalated twice or more multiple times escalated commissioner level list
sql_template:
SELECT c.complaint_number, c.title, c.escalation_level, COUNT(eh.id) AS times_escalated
FROM complaint c
JOIN escalation_history eh ON eh.complaint_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.complaint_number, c.title, c.escalation_level
HAVING COUNT(eh.id) >= 2
ORDER BY times_escalated DESC
LIMIT :limit;

question_template: How many escalated complaints are still pending?
retrieval_text: how many escalated complaints are still pending open unresolved even after escalation level list
sql_template:
SELECT c.complaint_number, c.title, c.escalation_level, d.department_name, w.ward_name
FROM complaint c
JOIN status_master s ON s.id = c.status_id AND s.is_terminal = false
LEFT JOIN department_master d ON d.id = c.department_id
LEFT JOIN ward_master w ON w.id = c.ward_id
WHERE c.escalation_level > 0
ORDER BY c.escalation_level DESC
LIMIT :limit;

question_template: What are the top {limit} complaint categories in Pune?
retrieval_text: what are the top complaint categories in pune potholes garbage dumping drainage overflow water supply streetlight

SELECT cat.category_name, cat.category_name_mar, COUNT(*) AS complaint_count
FROM complaint c
JOIN category_master cat ON cat.id = c.category_id

ORDER BY complaint_count DESC

question_template: Which category is rising fastest compared to last month?
retrieval_text: which category is rising fastest compared to last month surge increase monthly diff monsoon potholes
sql_template:
SELECT cat.category_name,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.created_at >= date_trunc('month', now())) AS this_month,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.created_at >= date_trunc('month', now()) - interval '1 month'
                          AND c.created_at < date_trunc('month', now())) AS last_month
FROM complaint c
JOIN category_master cat ON cat.id = c.category_id
GROUP BY cat.id, cat.category_name
ORDER BY (COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.created_at >= date_trunc('month', now())) -
          COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.created_at >= date_trunc('month', now()) - interval '1 month'
                             AND c.created_at < date_trunc('month', now()))) DESC
LIMIT :limit;

question_template: What is the average resolution time by category (slowest/fastest)?
retrieval_text: what is average resolution time by category slowest fastest category speed resolution days
sql_template:
SELECT cat.category_name,
       ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(epoch FROM (c.resolved_at - c.created_at))/86400)::numeric, 1) AS avg_days
FROM complaint c
JOIN category_master cat ON cat.id = c.category_id
WHERE c.resolved_at IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY cat.id, cat.category_name
ORDER BY avg_days DESC
LIMIT :limit;

question_template: Rank all 15 wards by pending complaints or resolution rate.
retrieval_text: rank all 15 wards by pending complaints resolution rate league table best worst ward ranking list

SELECT w.ward_name, w.ward_name_mar,
       COUNT(*) AS total,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.is_terminal = false) AS pending,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.status_code = 'RESOLVED') AS resolved,

question_template: Show zone wise complaint summary breakdown.

question_template: Show monthly complaint trend for received vs resolved.
retrieval_text: show monthly complaint trend for received vs resolved last 12 months monthly volume breakdown trend dakhva
sql_template:
SELECT date_trunc('month', c.created_at)::date AS month,
       COUNT(*) AS received,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.status_code = 'RESOLVED') AS resolved
FROM complaint c
JOIN status_master s ON s.id = c.status_id
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 DESC
LIMIT :limit;

question_template: Which day of the week gets the most complaints?

FROM complaint c

question_template: Any unusual spike or recent volume surge in complaints?
retrieval_text: any unusual spike or recent volume surge in complaints sudden increase last 30 days daily counts

question_template: Show daily complaint activity trend for the last {limit} days.
retrieval_text: show daily complaint activity trend for last days total received pending resolved count daily breakdown date wise complaints today open complaints daily summary

question_template: How many complaints were resolved citywide and average resolution time?
retrieval_text: how many complaints were resolved citywide average resolution time 48 hours same day resolution stats
sql_template:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_resolved,
       ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(epoch FROM (c.resolved_at - c.created_at))/86400)::numeric, 1) AS avg_days,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.resolved_at - c.created_at <= interval '48 hours') AS resolved_within_48h,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.resolved_at::date = c.created_at::date) AS same_day_resolved
FROM complaint c

question_template: Average resolution time department wise.
retrieval_text: average resolution time department wise which department resolves fastest slowest speed
sql_template:
SELECT d.department_name,

question_template: What is the average citizen satisfaction rating overall?
retrieval_text: what is the average citizen satisfaction rating overall feedback score 1 star 2 star negative feedback count
sql_template:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(f.rating)::numeric, 2) AS avg_rating,

FROM complaint_feedback f;

question_template: Which department gets the worst or best citizen feedback ratings?
retrieval_text: which department gets worst best citizen feedback rating satisfaction score department wise
sql_template:
SELECT d.department_name,
       ROUND(AVG(f.rating)::numeric, 2) AS avg_rating,

JOIN complaint c ON c.id = f.complaint_id
JOIN department_master d ON d.id = c.department_id

question_template: Show recent negative feedback comments with complaint numbers.

FROM complaint_feedback f
JOIN complaint c ON c.id = f.complaint_id

LIMIT :limit;

question_template: Show top complaint hotspots in the city (geographic clusters).
retrieval_text: show top complaint hotspots in the city geographic clusters location map lat lng density highest complaints area
sql_template:
SELECT ROUND(c.latitude::numeric, 3) AS lat,
       ROUND(c.longitude::numeric, 3) AS lng,
       COUNT(*) AS complaint_count,
       MIN(c.address) AS sample_address
FROM complaint c
WHERE c.latitude IS NOT NULL AND c.longitude IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1, 2
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
ORDER BY complaint_count DESC
LIMIT :limit;

question_template: Which locations have repeat complaints of the same type?
retrieval_text: which locations have repeat complaints of the same type same spot recurring garbage potholes issues
sql_template:
SELECT ROUND(c.latitude::numeric, 3) AS lat,
       ROUND(c.longitude::numeric, 3) AS lng,
       cat.category_name,
       COUNT(*) AS repeat_count
FROM complaint c
JOIN category_master cat ON cat.id = c.category_id
WHERE c.latitude IS NOT NULL AND c.longitude IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1, 2, cat.category_name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
ORDER BY repeat_count DESC
LIMIT :limit;

question_template: Give me the full scorecard picture of {department}.
retrieval_text: give me full picture scorecard of water supply health road drainage solid waste department pending resolved sla workload
sql_template:
SELECT d.department_name,
       COUNT(*) AS total_complaints,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.is_terminal = false) AS pending,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.status_code = 'RESOLVED') AS resolved,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.sla_status = 'BREACHED') AS sla_breached,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.escalation_level > 0) AS escalated,
       ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(epoch FROM (c.resolved_at - c.created_at))/86400)
             FILTER (WHERE c.resolved_at IS NOT NULL)::numeric, 1) AS avg_days
FROM complaint c
JOIN status_master s ON s.id = c.status_id
JOIN department_master d ON d.id = c.department_id
WHERE c.department_id = :department_id
GROUP BY d.id, d.department_name;

question_template: Show active officers and workload in {department}.
retrieval_text: show active officers and workload open assigned complaints in road water supply department
sql_template:
SELECT u.full_name, u.designation,
       COUNT(c.id) FILTER (WHERE s.is_terminal = false) AS open_assigned
FROM user_master u
LEFT JOIN complaint c ON COALESCE(c.assigned_to_id, c.ward_officer_id) = u.id
LEFT JOIN status_master s ON s.id = c.status_id
WHERE u.department_id = :department_id AND u.is_active = true
GROUP BY u.id, u.full_name, u.designation

question_template: Show aging bucket breakdown (0-7, 7-30, 30-90, 90+ days).
retrieval_text: show aging bucket breakdown 0-7 7-30 30-90 90+ days distribution pending open complaints age
sql_template:
SELECT CASE
         WHEN now() - c.created_at < interval '7 days'  THEN '0-7 days'
         WHEN now() - c.created_at < interval '30 days' THEN '7-30 days'
         WHEN now() - c.created_at < interval '90 days' THEN '30-90 days'
         ELSE '90+ days' END AS age_bucket,
       COUNT(*) AS pending_count
FROM complaint c
JOIN status_master s ON s.id = c.status_id AND s.is_terminal = false
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;

question_template: What are the {limit} oldest open complaints in the city?
retrieval_text: what are the oldest open complaints in the city 10 oldest pending complaints list details officer ward
sql_template:
SELECT c.complaint_number, c.title, c.created_at,
       EXTRACT(day FROM now() - c.created_at) AS age_days,
       d.department_name, w.ward_name, u.full_name AS assigned_officer, s.status_name
FROM complaint c
JOIN status_master s ON s.id = c.status_id AND s.is_terminal = false
LEFT JOIN department_master d ON d.id = c.department_id
LEFT JOIN ward_master w ON w.id = c.ward_id
LEFT JOIN user_master u ON u.id = COALESCE(c.assigned_to_id, c.ward_officer_id)
ORDER BY c.created_at ASC

question_template: Show complaints pending for more than 30 or 90 days.
retrieval_text: show complaints pending for more than 30 60 90 days older long pending backlog list

question_template: Show list of all PMC departments with complaint counts and resolution rates.
retrieval_text: give me the list of departments list all departments show all departments department list sarva vibhaganchi yadi department wise list all departments list
sql_template:
SELECT d.id AS department_id,
       d.department_name,
       d.department_name_mar,
       COUNT(c.id) AS total_complaints,
       COUNT(c.id) FILTER (WHERE s.is_terminal = false) AS pending_complaints,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(c.id) FILTER (WHERE s.status_code = 'RESOLVED') / NULLIF(COUNT(c.id), 0), 1) AS resolution_rate
FROM department_master d

question_template: Show channel wise resolution rate, complaint counts, and comparison across all channels (Call Center, Web, Mobile, Walk-in).
retrieval_text: how many complaints came from call center vs web vs mobile vs walk-in swachhata app channel distribution resolution rate konta channel best compare channels channel wise resolution rate sarva channel chi tulna all channels channel comparison चॅनेल तुलना सर्व चॅनेलची तुलना चॅनेल रिझोल्यूशन रेट
sql_template:
SELECT c.source_channel,
       COUNT(*) AS received,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.status_code = 'RESOLVED') AS resolved,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.status_code = 'RESOLVED') / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1) AS resolution_rate,

question_template: How many complaints were rejected and what are the rejection reasons?

question_template: Which officers are overloaded right now (workload score ranking)?
retrieval_text: which officers are overloaded right now workload score ranking open pending overdue assigned list
sql_template:
SELECT u.full_name, d.department_name,
       (COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.status_code IN ('REGISTERED','ASSIGNED','PENDING')) * 1.5 +
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.status_code = 'PROCESSING') * 1.0 +
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.sla_deadline < now() AND s.is_terminal = false) * 3.0) AS workload_score,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.is_terminal = false) AS open_count
FROM complaint c
JOIN status_master s ON s.id = c.status_id
JOIN user_master u ON u.id = COALESCE(c.assigned_to_id, c.ward_officer_id)
LEFT JOIN department_master d ON d.id = u.department_id
GROUP BY u.id, u.full_name, d.department_name
ORDER BY workload_score DESC
LIMIT :limit;

question_template: How many complaints are unassigned right now by department?
retrieval_text: how many complaints are unassigned right now department wise unassigned open count stuck
sql_template:
SELECT d.department_name, COUNT(*) AS unassigned_count
FROM complaint c
JOIN status_master s ON s.id = c.status_id AND s.is_terminal = false
LEFT JOIN department_master d ON d.id = c.department_id
WHERE c.assigned_to_id IS NULL AND c.ward_officer_id IS NULL
GROUP BY d.department_name
ORDER BY unassigned_count DESC;

question_template: Show wards where no L1 officer is mapped for a department.
retrieval_text: show wards where no l1 officer is mapped for a department coverage gaps staffing shortage
sql_template:
SELECT w.ward_name, d.department_name
FROM ward_master w
CROSS JOIN department_master d
WHERE w.ward_number IS NOT NULL AND d.is_active = true
  AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM department_ward_officer dwo
      WHERE dwo.ward_id = w.id AND dwo.department_id = d.id AND dwo.is_active = true
  )
LIMIT :limit;

question_template: What is the status of complaint {complaint_number}?
retrieval_text: what is the status of complaint cms number full details officer ward category sla remaining escalation level
sql_template:
SELECT c.complaint_number, c.title, s.status_name, s.status_name_mar,
       cat.category_name AS category, d.department_name, w.ward_name,
       u.full_name AS assigned_officer,
       c.created_at, c.sla_deadline,
       GREATEST(c.sla_deadline - now(), interval '0') AS sla_remaining,
       c.escalation_level, c.reopen_count
FROM complaint c
JOIN status_master s ON s.id = c.status_id
LEFT JOIN category_master cat ON cat.id = c.category_id
LEFT JOIN department_master d ON d.id = c.department_id
LEFT JOIN ward_master w ON w.id = c.ward_id
LEFT JOIN user_master u ON u.id = COALESCE(c.assigned_to_id, c.ward_officer_id)
WHERE c.complaint_number = :complaint_number;

question_template: Show full action history of complaint {complaint_number}.
retrieval_text: show full history action history timeline events taken for complaint cms number
sql_template:
SELECT h.created_at, h.action_type, h.remarks, u.full_name AS by_officer
FROM complaint_action_history h
JOIN complaint c ON c.id = h.complaint_id
LEFT JOIN user_master u ON u.id = h.performed_by_id
WHERE c.complaint_number = :complaint_number
ORDER BY h.created_at ASC;
